context: Small-multiples force-directed network graph showing network topology evolution across 6 months (Jan–Jun), with edges classified as new (green), removed (dashed pink), or persistent (gray).
first_impression: Honest encoding for a topology visualization — no spatial scale deception, correct use of distinct visual channels for edge status, and proper node key functions.
what_works: Node joins use `.data(pd.nodes, d => d.id)` for correct object constancy; edge status is encoded through genuinely distinct channels (hue + dash pattern) with no conflation; per-panel stats (nodeCount, edgeCount) give honest quantitative anchors.
what_doesnt: Each panel runs an unseeded, independent force simulation so the same node can appear in wildly different positions across months, making cross-panel topology comparison unreliable (acknowledged in subtitle but structurally unavoidable); link selections lack key functions (`.data(pd.links)`) which would corrupt animated updates if the link set were ever patched rather than rebuilt.
